claims.text: Aurora Avenue North had 78 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.3 million a year (injury crashes only: deaths are not valued in this figure).
16% of crashes here were recorded as “from same direction - both going straight - one stopped - rear-end” crashes, against 9% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons would avoid about 1.3 crashes a year (CMF 9024, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $454,000 a year.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 2.2 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $757,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for Aurora Avenue North (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).
A request letter to the state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is ready to draft from these facts.
